sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Hart County, KY?
sections.html:
Three courthouse-area offices touch a Hart County tax bill: the Property Valuation Administrator sets the assessed value, the sheriff collects the money, and the county clerk keeps the deed records and takes over unpaid bills. All three sit in Munfordville, the county seat.

  • The Hart County PVA mails to P.O. Box 566, Munfordville, KY 42765, and answers at (270) 524-2321 from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday through Friday.
  • The sheriff's office is at 100 Main Street, Munfordville, with a phone line at (270) 524-2341. The county's sheriff page points owners to hartcountysheriffky.com for paying bills online.
  • The county clerk is at 200 Main Street, Munfordville, (270) 524-2751. The office is open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. and on Saturday mornings from 9 a.m. to noon.

Kentucky law makes the sheriff the collector of state, county, school and special district property taxes under KRS 134.119. The sheriff can take full or partial payments from the day bills are mailed until the uncollected claims go to the clerk, and a third party may pay on an owner's behalf.

sections.h2: What is Hart County like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Hart County is a rural, cave-country county in south central Kentucky, and 88.3 percent of residents lived in rural areas at the 2020 census. The county was formed in 1819 from parts of Hardin and Barren counties, covers 418 square miles, and has two incorporated cities: Munfordville, the seat, and Horse Cave, the largest.

The landscape drives part of the housing picture. A slice of Mammoth Cave National Park lies in the west of the county, and the Fisher Ridge Cave System, mapped to about 125 miles as of 2018, runs under Hart County ground. An Amish settlement founded in 1989 between Munfordville and Horse Cave counted 2,486 residents in 2020, about 12.9 percent of the population.

The Battle of Munfordville was fought in the county in 1862, and a courthouse fire in January 1928 destroyed some county records. Sellers of older farms who find a gap in their paperwork can ask the county clerk what survives for their parcel.

The county sits in the Central time zone, and Wikipedia's county profile marks the northern lines with Hardin and LaRue counties as the Eastern time border. Check which clock a closing office uses before you set a signing time.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Hart County housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates describe a low-cost, mostly owner-occupied market. Nearly three out of four homes are lived in by their owners, and the typical value is well under the state's larger metro areas.

sections.h2: When does a Hart County tax bill become late?
sections.html:
A Hart County bill turns late after December 31 of the assessment year, and the cost of waiting climbs in two steps. The calendar comes from KRS 134.015.

  • Pay in full by November 1 and the bill drops by 2 percent.
  • Pay from November 2 through December 31 and you owe the printed amount.
  • Pay during January and a 5 percent penalty applies.
  • Pay after January 31 and the penalty is 10 percent.

If the state delays bill production, the Department of Revenue can substitute a shorter schedule counted from the mailing date. The statute also makes unpaid tax a personal debt of whoever owned the parcel on January 1.

The Hart County PVA's office is the place to learn who is listed as the owner on that date, because assessment follows ownership on January 1 and not the closing date. A buyer who closes in the spring should expect the first bill to arrive in the seller's name and should settle that cost at the table.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Hart County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with a conference at the PVA's office, then take the case to the county board of assessment appeals if the value still looks wrong. The steps are set out in KRS 133.120, which the legislature amended effective July 15, 2026.

  1. Ask the PVA or a deputy for a conference before or during the tax roll inspection period. A phone conference is allowed if you ask for one.
  2. The PVA must explain how your value was derived and keep a written record of what each side said.
  3. If you still disagree, file a written petition with the Hart County Clerk by one workday after inspection ends. Say why you object, identify the parcel, and state what you think it is worth.
  4. Appear at the board hearing with evidence such as listings, sales, insurance records, construction cost or a mortgage. A petition that lacks supporting facts is denied.

The board meets between 25 and 35 days after inspection closes under KRS 133.030, and it must inspect the property in person if you or the PVA ask. You may record the hearing. An appeal does not pause the bill: you pay tax on the value you claim, and the balance is billed later if the board lands higher.

sections.h2: Can Hart County homeowners get a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Yes, if you are at least 65 or are classified as totally disabled and the house is your home. The Kentucky Department of Revenue sets the 2025 and 2026 exemption at $49,100, subtracted from the assessed value before the tax rate is applied.

On a home assessed at $146,000, the Census median for Hart County, the taxable assessment would fall to $96,900. File the application with the Hart County PVA; proof of age can be a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Disability claims need a federal or retirement-system classification, and most must be renewed each year unless the owner is a service-connected veteran or has a permanent Social Security or state retirement ruling.

When you sell, tell the PVA so the exemption stops at your old address and the buyer, if eligible, can apply for their own.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid taxes when a Hart County house sells?
sections.html:
The debt follows the parcel. Under KRS 134.015(5), a lien for delinquent tax continues under KRS 134.420 for up to eleven years no matter who owns the property, so a title search will turn it up and the buyer's lender will want it cleared.

Call the sheriff for a payoff figure before listing. Once the sheriff files unpaid claims with the county clerk, the bill grows by clerk and sheriff charges set in KRS 134.119, including a collection fee of ten percent of the tax plus ten percent of the penalty. Someone can then buy the certificate of delinquency and add their own interest.

Owners who sell a Hart County farm or house with a tax lien usually pay it from the proceeds at closing. A seller who cannot pay up front should ask the title company to hold the payoff from the sale amount.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a Hart County deed?
sections.html:
Kentucky charges the seller a real estate transfer tax of fifty cents for each $500 of value or fraction, collected by the clerk before a deed is accepted for recording, under KRS 142.050. On a $146,000 sale the tax is $146.

The Hart County Clerk's office, at 200 Main Street in Munfordville, keeps the county's land records. The statute exempts transfers such as those between spouses in a divorce, foreclosure sales, and parent-to-child deeds for nominal consideration. Ask the clerk for the current recording charge before you submit the deed.

faqs.q: Who sends property tax bills in Hart County, Kentucky?
faqs.a: The sheriff's office sends and collects them. The PVA supplies the assessment and the county clerk takes over bills the sheriff does not collect. Contact the sheriff at (270) 524-2341 if you have not received a bill.

faqs.q: What is the Hart County homestead exemption worth?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 off the assessed value for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. You must be 65 or older, or totally disabled, and apply with the Hart County PVA at (270) 524-2321.

faqs.q: Is there a discount for paying early in Hart County?
faqs.a: Yes, 2 percent if the bill is paid in full by November 1 of the assessment year. After December 31, penalties of 5 percent and then 10 percent apply under KRS 134.015.

faqs.q: Does an assessment appeal delay my Hart County tax payment?
faqs.a: No. KRS 133.120 requires you to pay tax on the value you claim while the appeal is pending. If the final value is higher, you are billed the difference with interest.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hart County house that still owes taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, but the lien stays with the parcel until it is paid. Get a payoff from the sheriff and have the title company pay it from your proceeds at closing.
